title: GDScript: Fix indexing type checks for Quaternion and Transform3D

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
Fixes #120318

The issue thread basically had the whole solution mapped out by AThousandShips and kleonc, so I just went ahead and implemented what they described. 

Basically, `Quaternion[0]` was throwing an analyzer error in GDScript even though `operator[](int)` is exposed and documented. If you look in `gdscript_analyzer.cpp` (`reduce_subscript`), `QUATERNION` was grouped under "Expect String only". Meanwhile, other types like Vector*, Basis, Color, and Transform2D were sitting in the "Expect String or number" group.

`TRANSFORM3D` had the exact opposite problem. It was in the "Expect String or number" group, but it doesn't even expose `operator[]` in 4.x. Because of that, `t[0]` parsed perfectly fine and only crashed at runtime, which is a lot more confusing than a straightforward analyzer error.

I swapped these two cases around and added two tests:
* `analyzer/features/quaternion_index_int.gd` to check that `Quaternion[0]` parses correctly.
* `analyzer/errors/transform3d_index_int.gd` to make sure `Transform3D[0]` produces a clear analyzer error.

I kept the tests under `analyzer/` since the error path is `GDTEST_ANALYZER_ERROR`, but I can totally move them to `parser/` if that fits your workflow better. All GDScript tests are passing locally.

By the way, this is my first PR to Godot! I'm coming from Unity, so I just used Claude to quickly get up to speed on the engine's contribution guidelines and test structures, but the actual fix was straightforward thanks to the awesome diagnosis in the issue. Built and verified everything locally. Also used Claude to create this description since English isn't my first language.
